A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NovelHopQA and contain readable text, tables, figures, and appendices. The original examples, validation form, and prompts can be matched across appendix renumbering; v2 adds a new RAG appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-model evaluations, human validation, and irrelevant/no-context experiments in Tables 1–3, 6, and 11.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds LLaMA evaluations and seven-model RAG results in Table 13.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 expands the stated golden-context acceptance filter from success by all six models to all seven, including LLaMA. Keyword selection, paragraph chaining, and QA generation remain unchanged. Appendix B reports unchanged removal counts, so changed dataset membership is not established.

E1.justification: The 83 English novels, hop depths, and long-context coverage remain unchanged. Appendix F adds a retrieved-passage scenario in which models receive approximately 2.5k tokens of potentially incomplete evidence instead of the full narrative window.

E2.justification: LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct joins the golden-context, full-context, and irrelevant/no-context comparisons in Tables 1, 3, and 11. Table 13 additionally introduces BGE/FAISS retrieval-augmented variants of all seven models, substantially extending the comparison methods beyond direct context prompting.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces a new evaluation protocol: index full novels in non-overlapping 350-token chunks, retrieve seven chunks by inner-product similarity, concatenate them in original order, and evaluate the resulting short context. The existing context-length grid, human annotation procedure, and stated CoT/GPT-4.1 grading practice are retained.

E4.justification: The new retrieved-context comparison probes whether selected, potentially incomplete passages support multi-hop answering. Existing irrelevant/no-context controls also cover LLaMA. Appendix D's four failure examples remain unchanged; the proposed RAG failure mechanisms are discussed without separate coverage or ordering ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model accuracy. Human-validator reporting remains unchanged, and the new results introduce no uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds LLaMA results across the existing evaluations and a complete RAG result table. LLaMA scores 64.42% at 128k/4 hops; RAG mean accuracy decreases from 54.69% at one hop to 43.82% at four hops. The original six-model table entries remain unchanged; aggregate averages change when LLaMA is included.

T1.justification: The chaining notation and mathematical description are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new retrieval procedure introduces no substantive formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion add RAG evaluation to the stated contributions, and the empirical study expands from six to seven models. The central novelty claim and conclusion that larger context windows do not ensure reliable multi-hop reasoning remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly attributes retrieval failures to incomplete hop coverage and evidence misalignment, arguing that retrieval cannot replace full-context comprehension. Section 5 also adds interpretations of LLaMA's robustness. The existing limitations and original failure-mode interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents BGE/FAISS retrieval settings, adds LLaMA's API provider, and changes the Azure provider description to AI Foundry. The abstract and conclusion add a project access link and claim code/data availability, although the reproducibility statement still promises release upon publication. Generation prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: References to BGE, FAISS, and LLaMA are added for the new experiments. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing long-context and multi-hop benchmarks are otherwise substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, results discussion, and conclusion; updates affiliations and contact information; and adds acknowledgements. A new Appendix F shifts the original appendices F–H to G–I without substantially reorganizing the existing narrative.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 11 expand for LLaMA, and Figures 2–4 are redrawn with additional model series, reordered panels, and changed axes or colors. The heatmap loses numerical cell annotations. A new RAG table and two-panel figure are added, while existing appendix examples and forms are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful model coverage, RAG results, and implementation details, but introduces material reporting inconsistencies. Section 5 claims LLaMA outperforms Flash at higher hops, although Table 3 shows lower LLaMA scores at every three- and four-hop setting. Appendix F states a 25–35-point golden-context deficit, whereas Tables 1 and 13 report overall averages differing by 44.80 points. The broader evidence and weaker reporting consistency leave the net quality change uncertain.
